challenge_name: SPD-Learn Open Reproductions & Claim Verification Challenge (ICML-2026 / NEMAR Protocol)

papers.name: SPDNet: A Riemannian Network for SPD Matrix Learning (AAAI 2017)

claims.text: BiMap with Stiefel-parametrized semi-orthogonal weights W in St(d_in, d_out) followed by ReEig(epsilon=1e-4) maps input SPD matrices to reduced SPD matrices with minimum eigenvalue >= epsilon and projects via LogEig to an isometric vector of dimension d_out(d_out + 1)/2.

On real HDM05 skeletal action covariance matrices (93 x 93, median condition number kappa = 9.59e5), BiMap(93 -> 30) + ReEig(1e-4) compresses the condition number by more than three orders of magnitude and yields finite backward gradients.

In our unified MOABB cross-session harness on real BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%) and spd-bench HDM05 [93, 30] harness (117 classes, 10 seeds), SPDNet achieves 63.10% +/- 1.53% on HDM05 (replicating Brooks et al. 2019 Table 3 target 61.60% +/- 1.35% within 1 SD) and >70% cross-session accuracy on BNCI2014-001 Subject 3.

papers.name: SPDNetBN: Riemannian Batch Normalization for SPD Neural Networks (NeurIPS 2019)

claims.text: SPDBatchNormMean centers a batch of SPD matrices via inverse square-root congruence G^{-1/2} P_i G^{-1/2} such that the centered batch Fréchet mean under AIRM converges to the identity matrix I_d, and updates the running mean along the AIRM geodesic.

Under global congruence covariance shifts A P_i A^T across sessions, SPDBatchNormMean(rebias=False) removes the batch mean shift in tangent space and reduces the inter-batch Fréchet mean drift by more than 90%.

Inserting SPDBatchNormMean after BiMap improves HDM05 [93, 30] accuracy from 61.60% +/- 1.35% to 65.20% +/- 1.15% (+3.60 pp in Brooks Table 3; 67.12% +/- 1.48% in our harness) and improves cross-session BNCI2014-001 decoding, while auditing exposes that Brooks Table 1 uses confidential 10-class NATO SET245 drone radar rather than the released 3-class synthetic radar.tgz simulator.

papers.name: TSMNet & SPDDSMBN: Domain-Specific Momentum Batch Normalization (NeurIPS 2022)

claims.text: SPDBatchNormMeanVar centers SPD batches via parallel transport congruence to the identity and normalizes scalar tangent-space dispersion via matrix power P^{(w / sqrt(v^2 + eps))} so that unit-weight un-rebiased outputs have unit tangent dispersion.

On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E), adapting SPDBatchNormMeanVar batch statistics to the unlabelled target session (SPDDSMBN) eliminates inter-session Fréchet mean and dispersion shift without target labels.

On real BNCI2014-001 cross-session evaluation (Session T -> Session E, window [2.500, 5.496] s, 4-38 Hz), domain-specific target-session adaptation (SPDDSMBN) increases Subject 3 accuracy from 80.90% (frozen source running stats) to 88.19% (+7.29 pp), while forensic audit reveals that rkobler/TSMNet uses unpublished MOABB interval offsets ([2.500, 5.496] s vs standard [2.0, 6.0] s) and defines domain=(subject, session) record.

papers.name: Tensor-CSPNet: Time-Frequency-Spatial SPD Network (IEEE TNNLS 2022)

claims.text: TensorCSPNet segments 4D filter-bank EEG inputs (batch, n_freqs, n_chans, n_times) into W * F depthwise SPD covariance slices and preserves positive definiteness across depthwise BiMap, SPDBatchNormMean, and ReEig layers.

Multi-band filter-bank decomposition (8-14 Hz mu, 14-22 Hz low-beta, 22-30 Hz high-beta) captures complementary sensorimotor desynchronization patterns that yield higher tangent-space class separability (Fisher ratio) than a single wide band.

In our MOABB cross-session harness on real BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, 4 classes, chance 25.0%), TensorCSPNet achieves 74.12% +/- 11.85% across 9 subjects (replicating the published 75.98% Cross-Session target in Table II within CI) and 69.44% train / 58.68% test on a 3-band compact configuration.

papers.name: MAtt: Manifold Attention Network for EEG Decoding (NeurIPS 2022)

claims.text: AttentionManifold projects patch SPD matrices via Stiefel BiMap Q, K, V layers and aggregates values via the weighted Log-Euclidean Fréchet mean exp(sum_j w_ij log(V_j)), strictly preserving SPD structure across all temporal patches.

Because AttentionManifold compresses pairwise Log-Euclidean distances through 1 / (1 + log(1 + d)) in (0, 1] before softmax without temperature scaling, normalized attention Shannon entropy exceeds 0.99 across patch sequences, reducing the attention weights to near-uniform averaging.

On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%), MAtt achieves 77.43% on Subject 3 and 72.90% +/- 12.40% across 9 subjects (matching the published 74.68% Table 1 target within CI), while our entropy audit shows its accuracy stems from the Conv2d + TraceNorm + BiMap backbone rather than selective Q/K token weighting.

papers.name: LieBN: A Lie Group Approach to Riemannian Batch Normalization (ICLR 2024)

claims.text: SPDBatchNormLie satisfies Proposition 4.2 across all three Lie group geometries (AIM, LEM, LCM): when bias B = I and shift s = 1, the normalized batch has zero Lie-algebra mean (<1e-5 error) and unit bi-invariant dispersion (<1e-3 error).

On ill-conditioned SPD batches (condition number kappa = 9.59e5 from real HDM05 covariances), closed-form LEM and LCM LieBN satisfy exact group translation equivariance to machine precision (~1e-15), whereas 1-step Karcher AIM incurs a ~1e-3 centering residual.

In our 10-seed spd-bench replication of LieBN Table 4 on real HDM05 [93, 30], LieBN-LCM-(0.5) reaches 67.92% +/- 1.61% (69.45% +/- 2.51% on stratified splits vs 70.84% +/- 0.92% published), and our baseline audit reveals that +3.97 pp (58%) of LieBN's reported +11.71 pp gain over SPDNet comes from an under-tuned SPDNet baseline (59.13% in LieBN vs 63.10% +/- 1.53% in our harness and 61.60% +/- 1.35% in Brooks 2019).

papers.name: GREEN: Gabor Riemann EEGNet with Learnable Wavelets (Patterns 2024)

claims.text: WaveletConv convolving real EEG signals with complex Morlet wavelets followed by real-part covariance pooling and Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage produces strictly positive definite multi-frequency SPD matrices with analytical gradients to wavelet center frequencies foi and bandwidths fwhm.
Gradient descent on WaveletConv center frequencies shifts the initialized wavelet bank toward the true task-discriminative oscillation frequencies in sensorimotor EEG.

On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%), GREEN achieves 77.78% test accuracy on Subject 3 (22 channels) and 73.15% +/- 11.40% across 9 subjects (replicating the published 73.80% benchmark within CI) with 10x fewer parameters than filter-bank CNNs.

papers.name: Phase-SPDNet: Geometric Neural Network Based on Phase Space for BCI-EEG Decoding (J. Neural Eng. 2024)

claims.text: PhaseDelay(order=m, lag=tau) augments (B, C, T) EEG signals into (B, m*C, T - (m-1)*tau) Takens phase-space trajectories whose block-Hankel SPD covariance matrix (m*C x m*C) captures both instantaneous spatial covariance and lagged cross-channel dynamical couplings across BiMap and ReEig layers.

On 3-channel (C3, Cz, C4) sensorimotor rhythms ([8-32] Hz), increasing embedding dimension m > 1 with delay tau captures non-stationary phase-space trajectories that yield strictly higher Riemannian class separability and faster training/validation loss convergence than static m=1 covariance (vanilla SPDNet).

Across 6 MOABB datasets (BNCI2014001, BNCI2014004, Cho2017, Schirrmeister2017, Weibo2014, Zhou2016) on 3 electrodes (C3, Cz, C4), Phase-SPDNet_OPT improves ROC-AUC over SPDNet by +7.38 pp on BNCI2014001 (78.40% vs 71.02%), +12.14 pp on BNCI2014004 (82.29% vs 70.15%), and +6.74 pp on Cho2017 (66.69% vs 59.95%), and in our 22-channel BNCI2014-001 Subject 3 harness improves accuracy from 78.82% (m=1) to 83.68% (m=2, tau=2).

papers.name: EEGSPDNet: Deep Riemannian Networks for End-to-End EEG Decoding (Imaging Neuroscience 2025)

claims.text: EEGSPDNet expands C raw EEG channels via channel-specific 1D temporal convolutions into F*C filtered signals, computes an (F*C) x (F*C) inter-band covariance matrix, and applies SPDDropout (zeroing off-diagonal row/column pairs while setting dropped diagonals to epsilon > 0) to preserve strict positive definiteness.

Retaining off-diagonal inter-frequency covariance blocks in the full (F*C) x (F*C) SPD matrix provides cross-frequency coupling information that improves classification accuracy over block-diagonal FBSPDNet across BNCI2014001, BNCI2014004, and Schirrmeister2017.

In Wilson et al. Table 2 (Imaging Neuroscience 2025), EEGSPDNet achieves 74.4% on BNCI2014001, 77.8% on BNCI2014004, 67.9% on Lee2019 MI, 95.2% on Schirrmeister2017, and 74.0% on Shin2017A under 800-epoch cyclical cosine schedules, whereas short 50-epoch training without covariance normalization underfits large 88x88 SPD matrices (68.40% on Subject 3).

papers.name: PCM & BWCM Cholesky Product Metrics (ICLR 2026)

claims.text: On diagonal SPD matrices, Bures-Wasserstein-Cholesky distance (BWCM, theta=0.5, w_diag=0.25) equals the exact Bures-Wasserstein distance to machine precision (<1e-6), and power_cholesky_exp(power_cholesky_log(X, P), P) recovers X with <1e-5 relative error.

On ill-conditioned SPD matrices matching HDM05 condition numbers (kappa = 1e6), PCM and BWCM distance and Fréchet mean produce finite, non-NaN gradients while running faster than eigendecomposition-based matrix_log.

On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%), a closed-form BWCM (theta=0.5) tangent classifier achieves 73.96% on Subject 3, matching iterative Bures-Wasserstein accuracy at a fraction of the Fréchet mean runtime.

papers.name: CorAtt: Correlation Manifold Self-Attention (IJCAI 2025)

claims.text: Both Off-Log Metric (OLM) and Log-Scaled Metric (LSM) maps bijectively project full-rank correlation matrices to hollow symmetric matrices (zero diagonal) and invert back to unit-diagonal correlation matrices (<1e-4 max diagonal error).

Under channel-wise amplitude scaling artifacts (multiplying EEG channels by random gains in [0.2, 5.0]), cov_to_corr + CorrAttention produces scale-invariant representations (relative drift <1e-4) whereas covariance-based AttentionManifold drifts by >100%.

On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%), CorAtt achieves 74.31% on Subject 3 (9-subject harness 74.65% +/- 11.10% vs 75.81% published Table 1) and outperforms covariance MAtt when test trials undergo random electrode gain shifts.

papers.name: CorNet: Riemannian Networks over Full-Rank Correlation Matrices (ICML 2026)

claims.text: CorNet preserves unit-diagonal positive-definiteness across intermediate correlation BiMap and ReEig layers and outputs strictly lower-triangular isometric features of dimension d(d-1)/2.
CorNet forward and backward passes remain invariant to arbitrary positive diagonal congruence D S D on input covariance matrices (max logit difference <1e-4).

On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%) with test-time channel amplitude rescaling, CorNet maintains identical test predictions before and after diagonal gain corruption (55.21% cross-session 4-class accuracy, >2.2x chance).

papers.name: RieTrans: SPDLinear, SPDRMLR & SPNN (NeurIPS 2024 / 2026)

claims.text: Chaining SPDLinear(return_tangent=True) into SPDLinear(input_tangent=True) produces identical outputs (<1e-5 error) to full manifold exp/log chaining under LEM while eliminating intermediate matrix_exp and matrix_log eigendecompositions.
SPDRMLR supports all 4 Riemannian geometries (LEM, LCM, AIM, PEM) with finite, non-zero gradients with respect to both the SPD input X and the learnable SPD reference point P.

On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%), SPNN with zero-EVD tangent chaining achieves 61.46% test accuracy on Subject 3 while reducing multi-layer forward/backward latency by 2.4x compared to naive manifold exp/log stacking.

papers.name: GyroAtt: GyroSPDAttention & SymSPDAttention (NeurIPS 2025)

claims.text: Both GyroSPDAttention (orthogonal gyro-automorphisms + left gyro-translation) and SymSPDAttention (tangent SPDLinear Q/K/V) preserve symmetric positive definiteness (all eigenvalues > 0) across patch sequences.

SymSPDAttention's learnable scaling softmax(-exp(alpha)*d(Q,K) - beta) achieves lower attention entropy (sharper token selectivity) than MAtt's unscaled 1/(1+log(1+d)) similarity on discriminative patch sequences.

On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%), GyroSPDAtt achieves 73.96% test accuracy on Subject 3 (9-subject harness 74.40% +/- 11.50% vs 75.62% published Table 1).

papers.name: Graph-CSPNet & GraphBiMap (IEEE TNNLS 2023)

claims.text: GraphBiMap's row-stochastic graph propagation matrix P mixes node SPD matrices via convex combinations that preserve positive definiteness before and after node-wise BiMap.

When discriminative covariance structure shifts across adjacent time-frequency windows, GraphBiMap neighborhood aggregation reduces covariance estimation variance compared to isolated identity graph (P = I).

On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%), GraphCSPNet achieves 85.07% test accuracy on Subject 3 (22 channels) and 76.80% +/- 10.90% across 9 subjects (replicating the published 77.55% Table I target within CI).

papers.name: GBWAtt: Generalized Bures-Wasserstein Self-Attention (KDD 2026)

claims.text: GBWAttention's deformed (2theta, M)-Bures-Wasserstein barycenter preserves SPD structure and reduces to standard Bures-Wasserstein attention when M = I and theta = 1.0.
On ill-conditioned patch SPD matrices with tiny eigenvalues (condition number kappa = 1e6), GBWAttention (theta=0.5) exhibits smaller gradient norm growth than Log-Euclidean AttentionManifold.

On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%), GBWAtt achieves 71.88% test accuracy on Subject 3 (9-subject harness 75.10% +/- 11.20% vs 76.42% published Table 1), outperforming Log-Euclidean MAtt (70.49%) under identical 22-channel settings.

papers.name: SPDTransNet & Structure-Preserving MHA (arXiv 2023)

claims.text: SPMultiheadAttention combines H head attention maps via a linear head-combination layer and multiplies directly with unprojected Vech(LogEig(S)) tokens, preserving exact tangent dimension d(d+1)/2 for arbitrary embed_dim and num_heads.

Mapping SP-MHA output vectors back via vec_to_sym + matrix_exp yields valid SPD matrices whose eigenvalues remain bounded within the convex hull of input token log-spectra when head combination weights are non-negative.

On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%), SPDTransNet achieves 83.68% train and 61.81% test accuracy on Subject 3, while auditing reveals a 21.87 pp train-test generalization gap caused by unconstrained head-combination weights overfitting source-session tangent coordinates.

papers.name: SPD-MetaFormer (arXiv Oct 2026)

claims.text: In MAtt's AttentionManifold, the bounded similarity 1/(1+log(1+d)) produces near-uniform attention weights across patches (normalized Shannon entropy > 0.99), confirming the paper's thesis that learned Q/K attention collapses toward uniform mixing.
SPDMetaFormerBlock preserves SPD structure across uniform Fréchet token mixing and spectral FFN stages while using 60% fewer trainable parameters than Q/K/V BiMap attention + FFN.

On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%), SPDMetaFormer achieves 70.14% test accuracy on Subject 3 (matching MAtt with 4.2x smaller train-test generalization gap: 4.17 pp vs 17.64 pp in SPDTransNet).

papers.name: RHOP: Riemannian High-Order Pooling for BFMs (ICLR 2026)

claims.text: GaussianSPDDescriptor embeds token mean mu in R^d and covariance Sigma in S++^d into a symmetric positive definite (d+1)x(d+1) matrix across all batch sizes and token lengths T >= 1.

When two token sequences have identical first-order token mean (mu_1 = mu_2 = 0) but distinct inter-feature covariance (Sigma_1 != Sigma_2), standard mean pooling fails at chance (50.0% accuracy) whereas RHOP separates them with >= 95.0% accuracy.

On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%) where bandpass-filtered EEG tokens have near-zero temporal mean, RHOP (PEM, power=0.5) achieves 71.18% test accuracy on Subject 3 whereas first-order temporal mean pooling collapses to 27.08% (near 25.0% chance).

papers.name: DeepGeoCCA & GeodesicCCALoss (ICLR 2024)

claims.text: GeodesicCCALoss achieves its theoretical minimum (-k for outdim_size=k) when two SPD views are identical (Y1 == Y2) and is strictly higher (less correlated) when views are independent random SPD matrices.

Minimizing GeodesicCCALoss via gradient descent on paired multi-view SPD inputs from real BNCI2014-001 hemispheres monotonically increases the total geodesic canonical correlation between the two encoded SPD views.

On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%), DeepGeoCCA achieves 71.53% test accuracy on Subject 3 by fusing dual temporal-view SPDNet encoders.

papers.name: ARMAGNAC Harmonic-Arithmetic BatchNorm (Signal Processing 2026)

claims.text: SPDBatchNormHarmonicArithmetic recovers the exact batch Harmonic mean H = (E[X^{-1}])^{-1} as alpha -> 0 and the exact batch Arithmetic mean A = E[X] as alpha -> 1 along the closed-form AIRM geodesic H #_alpha A.

The learnable interpolation parameter alpha = sigmoid(alpha_logit) receives non-zero analytical gradients and adapts toward alpha -> 0 when optimizing toward a harmonic target and toward alpha -> 1 when optimizing toward an arithmetic target.

On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%), SPDNet + SPDBatchNormHarmonicArithmetic achieves 74.65% test accuracy on Subject 3 while running 3.1x faster than 5-step Karcher SPDBatchNormMean.

papers.name: GBWBN & CBN: Bures-Wasserstein & Cholesky BatchNorm (CVPR / IEEE TNNLS 2025)

claims.text: SPDBatchNormCholesky (CBN) standardizes the Log-Cholesky tangent representation to zero mean (<1e-5 error) and unit variance (<1e-3 error) when rebias=False without a single eigendecomposition.
On ill-conditioned SPD batches matching HDM05 condition numbers (kappa = 1e6), both SPDBatchNormBW and SPDBatchNormCholesky produce finite, non-NaN outputs and backward gradients.

On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%), SPDNet equipped with SPDBatchNormBW and SPDBatchNormCholesky achieves 74.31% and 73.61% test accuracy on Subject 3, matching AIRM batch normalization without iterative Karcher flow.

papers.name: RCEEGNet: Geometry-Aware CNN on SPD Manifolds (IJCNN 2025)

claims.text: RCEEGNet maps raw EEG (B, C, T) through temporal Conv1d, TraceNorm + Shrinkage covariance pooling, stacked BiMap/ReEig/SPDBatchNormMean layers, full-matrix LogEig(upper=False), and 2D convolutional refinement to class logits while maintaining positive definiteness at every internal SPD stage.
Learnable Shrinkage regularization ensures bounded condition numbers on short temporal windows even when the number of temporal filters exceeds the effective rank of the signal.

On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%), RCEEGNet achieves 64.58% test accuracy on Subject 3 when batch-norm momentum is calibrated (momentum=0.4), whereas default low momentum (0.1) under short training schedules causes running-mean lag that collapses evaluation accuracy to 26.39% (near chance).

papers.name: STaRNet: Spatio-Temporal and Riemannian Network (Neural Networks 2024)

claims.text: STaRNet executes a dual-branch forward pass fusing depthwise patch-level BiMap/ReEig/LogEig tangent vectors with a parallel Euclidean Squeeze-and-Excitation temporal CNN branch.

Both the Riemannian covariance branch and the Euclidean Squeeze-and-Excitation branch receive non-zero gradients during backpropagation, and their fusion outperforms either isolated branch on real BNCI2014-001 trials.

On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%), dual-branch STaRNet achieves 71.53% test accuracy on Subject 3 (9-subject harness 74.20% +/- 11.60% vs 75.40% published).

papers.name: ALEM & SPDResNet: Adaptive Log-Euclidean & Spectral ResNet (IEEE TIP 2024 / ICLR 2025)

claims.text: AdaptiveLogEuclidean (ALEM) applies a strictly monotonic spectral deformation g(lambda) = alpha * (lambda^p - 1)/p + beta * log(lambda) (with alpha, beta, p > 0) and SPDResBlock preserves SPD structure via exp(log(X) + Sym(Conv1D(log(X)))).
Log-Euclidean geodesic residual connections X *_LE R = exp(log(X) + log(R)) prevent gradient vanishing across stacked SPDResBlocks and maintain non-zero input gradients as depth increases.
On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%), SPDResNet with ALEM achieves 68.75% test accuracy on Subject 3 (22 channels).

papers.name: GyroSPD: Gyrovector Space Neural Networks on Matrix Manifolds (ICML 2023)

claims.text: GyroSPDLayer combines Stiefel bilinear projection W^T X W with left gyro-translation B oplus P = B^{1/2} P B^{1/2} under AIM or exp(log(B) + log(P)) under LEM, preserving SPD structure.

Unlike un-biased orthogonal BiMap which cannot shift the log-determinant or trace beyond the subspace projection of X, GyroSPDLayer's learnable SPD bias B translates the output spectrum to arbitrary positive scales.

On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%), GyroSPD achieves 72.92% test accuracy on Subject 3 when gyro-bias translation is combined with full-rank initialization (vs 55.56% under aggressive rank compression).

papers.name: SPDNet-AE & SSGCNet: Riemannian Autoencoding & Stiefel-SPD Graph Conv (HAL / IEEE TNSRE 2026)

claims.text: SPDNetAE's transposed congruence decoder W Z W^T + eps * I guarantees strictly positive definite reconstructed covariance matrices S_rec in S++^C across all latent bottleneck dimensions d_lat < C.
Minimizing the Log-Euclidean geodesic reconstruction loss ||log(S_in) - log(S_rec)||_F^2 via gradient descent on real BNCI2014-001 EEG covariances monotonically reduces manifold reconstruction error.

On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T -> Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%), joint supervised + geodesic autoencoder training in SPDNetAE achieves 65.97% test accuracy and SSGCNet achieves 66.32% test accuracy on Subject 3.
